newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK TOBACCO FIRM LAUNCHES NEW ANTI-SMOKING FILTER.
newsitem.headline: GREEK TOBACCO FIRM LAUNCHES NEW ANTI-SMOKING FILTER.

text.p: Greek cooperative cigarette manufacturer SEKAP presented a new cigarette filter that it says will drastically reduce the risks of smoking, the company told a news conference on Wednesday.

"Smokers who use normal filters retain 1.75 ml of tar in their lungs. Bio-filter reduces this amount by 40 times, as was shown in experiments conducted on student smokers," said George Delikonstantinos, one of three professors who invented the filter.
He said the filter, which will be marketed by SEKAP in February, does not change the taste or smell of cigarettes, looks like normal filters but will be slightly more expensive.
"Bio-filter acts as an artificial lung, which retains all toxic substances and sends non-toxic smoke to the lungs. This is very significant for active and passive smokers," he added.
The 'bio-filter' which uses haemoglobin, the body's oxygen-carrier, has performed well in trials in screening out short-lived carcinogens that are not stopped by ordinary cigarette filters, he said.
Greeks are among the heaviest smokers in the world. --Margarita Sotiropoulou, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
